title: Welcoming Jaya Baloo as Cohere’s First CISO
gist: Cohere hired Jaya Baloo, AISLE co-founder and former CISO of Rapid7, Avast and KPN Telecom, as its first CISO. The company frames security and trust, not model capability, as the deciding factor in enterprise and government AI deployment, and uses the hire to back its pitch as a 'Sovereign AI platform'. AISLE's autonomous vulnerability-discovery record (500+ zero-days across 100+ codebases in its first year out of stealth) is cited as evidence that AI-native cybersecurity is maturing.

themes.theme: Trust as the enterprise AI buying criterion

insights.claim: Cohere argues that as AI becomes foundational infrastructure for governments and enterprises, buyers are weighing trust (whether systems can be trusted with sensitive data, critical operations and strategic assets) as heavily as model performance.
insights.speaker: Cohere
insights.so_what: If trust replaces benchmark scores as the deciding criterion, security-focused vendors like Cohere can compete with frontier labs without having the best model.
insights.quote: trust is becoming just as important as capability

insights.claim: According to Cohere, as organizations move AI from pilots into production, security, governance and compliance are becoming central requirements for deployment, especially for governments, critical infrastructure operators and highly regulated enterprises that need AI running inside their own environments and under their control.
insights.speaker: Cohere
insights.so_what: Moving from pilots to production in regulated sectors favors private or on-prem deployment and sovereign offerings over multi-tenant public APIs.
insights.quote: Security is the defining challenge of enterprise AI
insights.locator: Security is the defining challenge of enterprise AI

insights.claim: Cohere's stated strategy is to build 'the world's most trusted Sovereign AI platform': a complete stack that combines frontier models, agentic applications, secure deployment infrastructure and advanced cybersecurity capabilities, and that lets customers run AI wherever their data lives.
insights.speaker: Cohere
insights.so_what: Cohere is positioning itself as a sovereign and regulated-sector specialist rather than competing head-on on model capability, and is now adding cybersecurity as a pillar of the product.
insights.quote: successful AI deployment requires more than powerful models

insights.claim: Cohere appointed its first-ever Chief Information Security Officer, Jaya Baloo, in November 2026, and describes the hire as part of investing deeply in the people and technologies that let organizations deploy AI with confidence.
insights.speaker: Cohere
insights.so_what: A high-profile security executive is a credibility signal aimed at government and critical-infrastructure buyers; watch whether it is followed by security certifications or wins in regulated sectors.

insights.claim: AISLE, an AI-native cybersecurity company co-founded by Jaya Baloo, Ondrej Vlcek and Stanislav Fort, built autonomous AI systems that discover, validate and help remediate previously unknown vulnerabilities in production software, and found more than 500 such vulnerabilities across more than 100 codebases in its first year out of stealth.
insights.speaker: Cohere
insights.so_what: Autonomous zero-day discovery at this scale suggests AI could speed up both finding and fixing vulnerabilities, which would shift spending toward AI-native security tools.
insights.quote: identified more than 500 previously unknown vulnerabilities across more than 100 codebases
insights.locator: To solve this problem, AISLE developed

insights.claim: Cohere says a persistent problem in cybersecurity is that organizations can identify vulnerabilities but often cannot remediate them fast enough to stay ahead of attackers, and that autonomous AI is the fix.
insights.speaker: Cohere
insights.so_what: Spending may move from detection and scanning tools toward automated remediation, which is a risk for incumbent vulnerability-management vendors.
insights.quote: organizations can identify vulnerabilities, but often struggle to remediate them at the speed required to stay ahead of attackers

insights.claim: Jaya Baloo, Cohere's new CISO, argues that AI and cybersecurity are converging, and that as AI becomes part of critical infrastructure, security and trust need to be built in from the start rather than added later.
insights.speaker: Cohere
insights.so_what: Security that is designed into AI products from the start becomes a requirement to sell to critical-infrastructure buyers, which disadvantages vendors that add security after the fact.
insights.quote: As AI becomes part of critical infrastructure, security and trust need to be built in from the start, not added later.
insights.locator: Organizations are entering a new era

insights.claim: Cohere says cyber resilience, critical infrastructure security, vulnerability management and quantum readiness are becoming more important as agentic AI systems grow more capable and more deeply integrated into essential services.
insights.speaker: Cohere
insights.so_what: The spread of agentic AI enlarges the attack surface and pulls quantum readiness and infrastructure security into the AI security budget.
